title: Leafcutter Ants Have Farmed for 50 Million Years

scenes.text: Ants were farming fungus 50 million years ago.
Leafcutters slice leaves and carry them home like green sails.
They don't eat them. They feed them to a fungus garden underground.
The ants eat the fungus, which breaks down plant matter they can't digest.
Big workers cut leaves and small ones tend the garden.
Humans invented farming about ten thousand years ago. Ants beat us by millions.

description:
Leafcutter ants cut leaves to feed fungus gardens, a form of farming that scientists date back about 50 million years.
The ants eat the fungus, not the leaves.
What other animals do you think are farmers?
